Breakfast at the hotel.

Sightseeing tour of Cuenca.

Duration of the excursion day: 5–6 hours.
Altitude: 2,500 m above sea level.
Average temperature: approximately +25°C during the day and +12°C at night.

After breakfast, we will discover Cuenca, one of South America's most beautiful colonial cities. Thanks to its remarkably well-preserved historic center, where Spanish colonial architecture blends harmoniously with local traditions, the city was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1999.

Cuenca charms visitors with its cobbled streets, old mansions with elegant balconies, welcoming squares, numerous churches and peaceful atmosphere. The city's rich cultural heritage and its many distinguished writers, poets and artists have earned it the nickname “Athens of Ecuador.”

During the excursion, we will visit the city's principal landmarks: Abdón Calderón Square, the magnificent Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, one of the largest churches in Latin America, the picturesque Flower Square, San Francisco Square and the Turi viewpoint, which offers a splendid panorama of Cuenca.

We will also visit a famous workshop producing traditional “Panama hats.” Despite their name, these internationally renowned hats are made in Ecuador from toquilla palm fibers and are one of the country's symbols.

While strolling through the craft and fruit markets, you will have the opportunity to buy alpaca-wool products, silver jewelry, work by local artisans and other distinctive souvenirs.

Main stops: Abdón Calderón Square, the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, Flower Square, San Francisco Square, the riverfront, the Turi viewpoint, a Panama-hat factory, and the craft and fruit markets.

After the excursion, return to the hotel. Free time.

Today we will travel to Cuernavaca, known as the “City of Eternal Spring.” Located just an hour's drive from Mexico City, it is famous for its mild climate throughout the year.
Here we will visit the Palace of Cortés, a magnificent colonial building constructed by Hernán Cortés, as well as Cuernavaca Cathedral, the church of a former 16th-century Franciscan monastery.
We will then continue to Taxco, the famous “silver town,” a charming colonial town in the mountains of Guerrero state. Silver is a central part of its culture and economy.
Taxco's main landmark is the Church of Santa Prisca, an impressive Baroque church and one of Mexico's outstanding examples of religious architecture.
Holy Mass will be celebrated here.

This is a standalone route covering the listed monuments; visits to additional archaeological sites are arranged separately.

The Turismo Avalos tourist bus travels from Cusco to Puno through the high-altitude Andes. The route includes historic landmarks, a lunch stop and La Raya Pass.

In Andahuaylillas, you will visit the Church of San Pedro Apóstol, with its paintings, carved altars and colonial decoration. In Raqchi, you will see the remains of the Temple of Viracocha, dwellings and storage buildings within the Inca complex.

The bus stops for lunch in Sicuani. La Raya Pass lies at an elevation of approximately 4,300–4,400 meters, offering views of the mountains and Andean plateaus; a small local craft market operates nearby. In Pukara, the route introduces you to the heritage of a pre-Inca culture.

Arrival in Puno is expected at approximately 18:00, followed by a transfer to the hotel. Specific accommodation depends on the selected tour package.

Instead of the bus, you can choose the separate Titicaca Train option. The supplement is $295 per person, with departures on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays according to the operator's schedule. The train has a dining car, a bar and a panoramic carriage; a stop at La Raya and a three-course lunch are included. The bus route's stops are not guaranteed on the train option.
